sanjay: Heads-up — Helios (dedicated pool, eu-west-1) is seeing p95 spikes up to ~420ms over the last 24h even though token throughput is steady. My quick profile shows a large fraction of micro-batches (1–2 tokens) and a KV cache hit-rate regression after the rtx-kernel patch. Can we propose a tenant-scoped token-budget + queue-ceiling tweak for their dedicated capacity?

olivia: Can you paste the profiler numbers you saw? Also which pipeline is affected (generate vs chat vs embed)?

sanjay: generate/chat both affected, chat is worst. Profiler snippet (last 24h):
```
batch_size_distribution:
  1 token: 52%
  2 tokens: 24%
  3-7 tokens: 19%
  >=8 tokens: 5%
kv_cache_hit_rate:
  baseline (pre-rtx): 0.88
  current: 0.79  # ~9% drop
latency_by_route:
  /v1/chat.generate p95: 120ms -> 420ms
  /v1/text.generate p95: 95ms -> 280ms
queue_time_ms median: 8ms -> 24ms
```
Command I used: `/ops/profiler run --customer helios --since 24h --buckets batch_size,kv_hit,p95`

lucas: Ok. We should propose concrete adjustments and a canary plan + rollback criteria. What are you thinking for token budget and queue limits?

sanjay: Proposed tenant override (applies only to Helios dedicated pool):
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "helios",
  "overrides": {
    "token_budget": 1200,            // increase from default 800 to reduce microbatching
    "queue_ceiling_per_shard": 10,   // cap concurrent slices per shard
    "slice_target_ms": 60,           // make slices slightly larger to favor batch formation
    "max_batch_delay_ms": 12        // allow small additional queuing without hurting p50
  }
}
```
Rationale: larger token budget encourages batch aggregation while queue_ceiling prevents head-of-line fairness issues. The slice_target increase helps get fewer tiny batches.

anita: Two asks: 1) tighten `max_batch_delay_ms` to 10ms (12ms might hurt interactive SLAs) and 2) add canary throttles so the change only applies to 1 node (10% of pool) for 90m. Rollback criteria: p95 increase > 20% over baseline or KV hit-rate drop > 5% relative. Also add an alert for request queue growth > 3x baseline.

perf-bot: new flamegraph uploaded: https://perf.redwood.internal/helm/helios/2123456789/flamegraph.svg (shows kernel-level scatter around attention kernels post-rtx).

deploy-bot: Canary job created: `canary-hel-001` (applies override to node eu-west-1-a-03). Monitoring window 90m.

lucas: :+1: Also run `./tools/perf-check --customer helios --prepost` to capture pre/post KV hit and batch dist. If `p95_post > p95_pre * 1.2` OR `kv_hit_post < kv_hit_pre - 0.05` then auto-rollback. Add a temporary sampling of full request traces for the canary.

sanjay: Agreed. I'll update the override to `max_batch_delay_ms: 10` and schedule the canary then. Will attach pre-run metrics snapshot before toggling.

olivia: I'll run the canary and post the `perf-check` output in this thread. Expected timeline: start in ~15m, monitor, report after 90m.

anita: Please ensure oncall is pinged if alerts fire: @oncall-runtime. Also add a short note for Helios customer engineering so they expect minor latency variability during canary.

sanjay: Done — creating PR with the override and the canary config, assigning to olivia for rollout. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/helios-token-override (will link perf-check artifacts).

olivia: Starting canary now. Posting initial pre-run snapshot in 5m.

(ongoing, will update thread with perf-check outputs and flamegraphs)
